extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants and donors interested in longtermist / existential risk funding (AI safety, biorisk, institutional reform)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for applicants and donors for the Effective Altruism Long-Term Future Fund — what the fund seeks to support and what kinds of projects/activities are a good fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects that directly contribute to reducing existential risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund intends to support "Projects that directly contribute to reducing existential risks through technical research, policy analysis, advocacy, and/or demonstration projects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit focus on work addressing existential risks (examples given elsewhere on the page: advanced artificial intelligence and pandemics). Types of work include technical research, policy analysis, advocacy, and demonstration projects that have a plausible pathway to reducing global catastrophic risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for training, recruitment, and infrastructure for practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund intends to support "Training for researchers or practitioners who work to mitigate existential risks, or help with relevant recruitment efforts, or infrastructure for people working on longtermist projects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants can fund career-development activities, stipends, training programs, recruitment efforts, and infrastructure that help grow and sustain the community of people working on longtermist problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting long-term thinking and advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund supports "Promoting long-term thinking" and advocacy to increase awareness and concern for the long-term future among key stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes grants aimed at advocacy, outreach, public engagement, and influencing institutions (academia, government, industry) to take longtermist considerations seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad remit to promote, implement, and advocate for longtermist ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund has a "broad remit to make grants that promote, implement and advocate for longtermist ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fund is intentionally wide in scope within the longtermist domain and not limited to a single intervention type; applicants should frame how their work promotes longtermist aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcomes applications on long-term institutional reform and other global catastrophic risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund states it "welcomes applications related to long-term institutional reform or other global catastrophic risks (e.g., pandemics or nuclear conflict)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond AI, the fund is open to projects addressing institutional change and other GCRs; applicants should explain relevance to long-term future risk reduction or institutional resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding infrastructure, tools, and community-building activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund has funded work that "Created an instruction-generalization benchmark for LLMs," "Built and maintained digital infrastructure for the AI safety ecosystem," "Conducted public and expert surveys on AI governance and forecasting," and "Ran a biorisk summit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly supportive of building technical benchmarks, digital infrastructure, research platforms, surveys, convenings, and community-building initiatives that seed or strengthen the longtermist ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to fund stipends, salaries, and operational expenses for individuals and nascent organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured grants include individuals/early projects receiving stipends and salaries (e.g., "6-month stipend to create language model (LM) tools to aid alignment research", "1-year stipend to make videos and podcasts about AI Safety/Alignment, and build a community", "6 month salary & operational expenses to start a cybersecurity & alignment risk assessment org").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund will provide direct support for people (stipends/salaries) and cover operational costs for early-stage projects and organizations; applicants should justify how the funding will enable high-impact work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for low-tractability, long-horizon projects relying on proxy measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The page acknowledges: "Donors might conclude that improving the long-term future is not sufficiently tractable... It is very difficult to know whether actions taken now are actually likely to improve the long-term future. To gain feedback on their work, organizations must rely on proxy measures of success: Has the public become more supportive of their ideas? Are their researchers making progress on relevant questions?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund accepts that many supported activities will have uncertain causal pathways to long-term outcomes and will rely on proxy indicators of progress. Applicants should be explicit about their proxies and plausible causal chains; donors seeking strong short-term feedback loops may prefer other funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor-facing fit considerations / reasons not to donate
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists reasons why someone might choose not to donate (numbered 01–07): e.g., you don't think we should focus on the long-term future; you don't think future or possible beings matter; preference for supporting more established organizations; pessimism about room for more funding; identification of more promising projects; skepticism of AI risks; different views about how to improve the long-term future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items describe misalignment between donor preferences and the Fund's remit; applicants and donors should use these as negative fit indicators when deciding engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund manager expertise and contactability
rubrics_metrics.description: The page states: "Most of our fund managers have built their careers working full time in areas directly relevant to the Fund’s mission." and provides contact: "The Fund managers can be contacted at longtermfuture[at]effectivealtruismfunds.org"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can expect experienced fund managers; they may contact the fund managers for inquiries. This implies the Fund values domain expertise in both applicants and its own managers.
